sermon.title: Moral Advancement
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: After Moral Mutiny, Pastor David G. Kincer shows Hezekiah encouraging moral advancement: removing idols, opening to God’s word, resisting Assyria, cleansing the temple with the Levites, inviting negligent Israel, and seeing the people themselves destroy high places. He applies this to America—rejecting faith-without-repentance excuses, citing sexual-revolution costs as spoken, and urging united prayer because Jesus is greater than military might.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: STD statistics and homosexual-agenda dating (~1972) as spoken/unverified. Sensitive: homosexuality, divorce on demand, Iran/North Korea threats. Series Part 2 after Moral Mutiny.

chunks.section_question: What happened when the people met God under Hezekiah?
chunks.short_answer: The people broke sacred pillars, cut wooden images and threw down high places until destroyed—not only Hezekiah. One man started it but it did not stay one man. 2 Kings 19:14: Hezekiah prayed in God’s house. United seeking God can do more in America than capability alone; Jesus is greater than bombs and carriers.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And Hezekiah received the letter from the hand of the messengers, and read it; and Hezekiah went up to the house of the LORD, and spread it before the LORD. Then Hezekiah prayed before the LORD, and said: “O LORD God of Israel, the One who dwells between the cherubim, You are God, You alone, of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth. Incline Your ear, O LORD, and hear; open Your eyes, O LORD, and see; and hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to reproach the living God. Truly, LORD, the kings of Assyria have laid waste the nations and their lands, and have cast their gods into the fire; for they were not gods, but the work of men’s hands—wood and stone. Therefore they destroyed them. Now therefore, O LORD our God, I pray, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that You are the LORD God, You alone.”

faqs.question: Who followed Ahaz as king?
faqs.answer: Hezekiah his son reigned after Ahaz died and encouraged moral advancement instead of decline.

faqs.question: What empire did Hezekiah resist?
faqs.answer: Assyria, the big government/empire of that time trying to take over the world—he rebelled though he was a little nobody.

faqs.question: Are believers kings and priests toward the nation?
faqs.answer: From Revelation 5:10 Jesus has made us to our God kings and priests.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And have made us kings and priests to our God; And we shall reign on the earth.”

faqs.question: When does he say the homosexual agenda came out?
faqs.answer: He believes about 1972 or early seventies—an agenda for acceptance, marriage and related goals—as spoken.

faqs.question: Does faith and grace mean you can keep living in sexual sin?
faqs.answer: He rejects teaching that believing in Jesus lets you remain homosexual, adulterer or thief because God only looks through the blood of faith.

faqs.question: What adolescent STD rates does he cite?
faqs.answer: One out of four adolescents has an STD; fifty percent by age 25—statistics as spoken, unverified.

faqs.question: Why must helpers sanctify themselves first?
faqs.answer: Like the Levites cleansing themselves before God’s house, you set yourself apart before helping others in sin.

faqs.question: Must singing and praying include understanding?
faqs.answer: Everything must be with understanding because everything must edify and build people; Spirit and word together.

faqs.question: Did some mock Hezekiah’s Passover invitation?
faqs.answer: Some laughed, but some humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem and kept the Passover—worth sending the invitation.

faqs.question: Is Jesus greater than military power?
faqs.answer: He submits atomic bombs, jets and carriers are powerful, but we have something greater—Jesus Christ.
